Contactless electroreflectance (CER) spectroscopy was used to study the Fermi level position and band offsets in insulating (Ga,Mn)N/GaN structures.
For (Ga,Mn)N samples with Mn concentrations above 0.1%, the Fermi level was found to be strongly pinned in the middle of the band gap, at 1.25 - 1.55 eV above the valence band.
The Fermi level position was consistent across samples with different GaN cap thicknesses, indicating it is predominantly determined by the bulk properties of the (Ga,Mn)N layer.
The researchers estimated that most of the band gap change in (Ga,Mn)N, compared to GaN, occurs in the valence band, with a shift of -0.028 ± 0.008 eV per % Mn.
The insulating properties of (Ga,Mn)N, including strong Fermi level pinning and negligible surface depletion, make it a promising buffer material for nitride-based devices.
The undoped GaN cap layer provided a depletion-like region with a known width, allowing the built-in electric field and Fermi level position in the underlying (Ga,Mn)N layer to be determined.
The researchers assumed the Fermi level at the GaN surface was pinned at around 1.7 eV below the conduction band, based on previous studies of the surface density of states.
For samples with Mn concentrations above 0.1%, the CER signal showed a clear band-to-band transition followed by Franz-Keldysh oscillations, indicating a strong built-in electric field.
In contrast, the low-Mn sample (0.1% Mn) had a much weaker CER signal with an opposite phase Franz-Keldysh oscillation, suggesting the bands were bent in the opposite direction.
The strong Fermi level pinning, lack of a surface depletion layer, and high resistivity of (Ga,Mn)N make it a superior insulating buffer material compared to Fe- or C-doped GaN.
By assuming a fixed Fermi level position in (Ga,Mn)N, the researchers were able to estimate the valence band offset between GaN and (Ga,Mn)N to be -0.028 ± 0.008 eV per % Mn.

The low-temperature ferromagnetism observed in (Ga,Mn)N samples is likely due to superexchange Mn3+-Mn3+ coupling, as the Fermi level is pinned in the middle of the band gap and not conducive to carrier-mediated ferromagnetism.
The GaN/(Ga,Mn)N structures were grown by molecular beam epitaxy, with Mn concentrations ranging from 0.1% to 7%.
X-ray diffraction, secondary ion mass spectrometry, and superconducting quantum interference device magnetometry were used to characterize the structural and magnetic properties of the samples.
The thickness of the GaN cap layer was varied from 31 to 170 nm to study the effect on the built-in electric field and Fermi level position.
